items.title: Dimension of a product of locally algebraic schemes is the sum of the dimensions
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For locally algebraic k-schemes X and Y, the lemma shows that the dimension of the product at a point is the sum of the dimensions at the two projections, and consequently that the dimension of the product is the sum of the dimensions (statement lines 4004-4015). The proof factors the structure morphism of the product through Y, observes that the projection to Y is flat because it is a base change of the flat structure morphism of X over a field, identifies the dimension of the fibre over the image point with the dimension of X at the corresponding point, and then applies the additivity of fibre dimension along a flat morphism (proof lines 4018-4028). The global statement is an immediate consequence. The claim is H2: three cited inputs combined along one factorization, with no construction beyond choosing the right projection.
